issues.legal_issue: A borrower may seek tribunal review of a secured creditor’s enforcement measure when a possession notice has been issued, delivered, affixed, and published, without waiting for actual physical dispossession.
material_facts: The appeals arose from a ruling that a borrower could apply to the tribunal only after losing actual physical possession of the secured asset.

The dispute concerned whether the possession notice procedure, including delivery to the borrower, affixation at the property, and publication, itself constituted a measure that allowed an application for tribunal review.
The Supreme Court considered the statutory scheme governing enforcement measures and the tribunal’s authority to review them.
issues.conclusion: A borrower may approach the Debts Recovery Tribunal at the stage of a possession notice issued under Rule 8(1) and (2); actual physical possession is not a prerequisite. The contrary Full Bench ruling was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 13(4)(a) and 17(1) of the SARFAESI Act, read with Rules 8(1) and 8(2) of the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, taking possession includes the statutory mode of delivering and affixing a possession notice and publishing it. That mode is a measure under Section 13(4) capable of triggering the Section 17 remedy; the borrower need not first lose actual physical possession. Section 13(3-A) bars an application based merely on the communication of reasons for rejecting objections, but does not bar an application after a possession notice measure. Mardia Chemicals Ltd. v. Union of India established that the Section 17 remedy follows measures under Section 13(4). Transcore v. Union of India and Standard Chartered Bank v. V. Noble Kumar did not resolve the precise question of an application following the Rule 8(1) notice procedure. Canara Bank v. M. Amarender Reddy and ITC Limited v. Blue Coast Hotels Ltd. recognised symbolic or constructive possession within the statutory scheme.

rule.if: borrower_challenges_enforcement_measure and borrower_failed_to_pay_after_demand and possession_notice_delivered_and_affixed and possession_notice_published

predicates.borrower_challenges_enforcement_measure: The borrower brought a proceeding challenging a secured creditor’s enforcement measure.
predicates.borrower_failed_to_pay_after_demand: The borrower did not discharge the secured debt after the creditor demanded payment.
predicates.possession_notice_delivered_and_affixed: The creditor’s authorised officer delivered a possession notice to the borrower and affixed it at the property.
predicates.possession_notice_published: The creditor’s authorised officer published the possession notice for public notice.
predicates.borrower_may_apply_for_tribunal_review: The borrower may apply to the tribunal to review the creditor’s enforcement measure.

issues.definition: When a borrower challenges enforcement after failing to pay a demand and the creditor has delivered, affixed, and published a possession notice, the borrower may apply for tribunal review without first losing physical possession.
